Healthcare workers in the 51-100 patient volume group (number of patients seen: '51-100') show a statistically significant difference (p < 0.05) in COVID-19 severity between BCG vaccination and placebo based on chi-square analysis of COVID Health Status (AEHS, ambulatory [scores 0–2] vs. hospitalized [scores ≥3]: Pearson chi-square χ² = 4.7882, df = 1, p = 0.02865 for all COVID-19 cases; χ² = 4.5818, df = 1, p = 0.03231 for exact 'COVID-19' cases). 

Additionally, if COVID-19 severity is operationalized at the event level using adverse event severity grades (AESEV, mild/moderate [grades 1–2] vs. severe [grades 3–4]), the 1-50 patient volume group also shows a statistically significant uncorrected Pearson chi-square difference (χ² = 4.4417, df = 1, p = 0.03507). In contrast, the >100 patient volume group showed no statistically significant differences under any specification (all p > 0.35).
